Welcome to a journey where history meets the urgency of now—where questions of race, identity, and belonging are more than just ideas; they're lived, felt, and deeply personal.
Imagine walking through your own memories, while the world around you seems to press in with both its contradictions and its possibilities. That’s the heart of what we’ll explore together, inspired by the powerful reflections in Ta-Nehisi Coates’ Between the World and Me.
You’ll find that this isn’t just a story about struggle—it’s about facing the hard truths of systemic injustice and generational trauma, all while searching for meaning, connection, and a sense of home.
We’ll move from the intimate moments of childhood all the way to the sweeping currents of American history, tracing how the body and soul are shaped—and sometimes scarred—by the forces of culture and power.
Along the way, we’ll ask urgent questions: How do you find safety and dignity in a world that feels uncertain? What does it mean to truly belong? Through Coates’ lens, we’ll see that claiming your story, and your body, becomes not just a personal act, but something deeply communal.
While the road ahead may be uncertain, there’s resilience in bearing witness, and hope in seeking understanding together. So, let’s open our hearts and minds as we step into this exploration—ready to reckon with the world as it is, and imagine what it might yet become.
